title: N:M Sparse DNN Kernels for RISC-V MCUs via Custom ISA Extension
problem: N:M semi-structured sparsity cannot be efficiently exploited on RISC-V microcontrollers (MCUs) because standard ISAs lack the hardware primitives to accelerate structured sparse operations without prohibitive overhead.
motivation: Edge MCUs (IoT, wearable, embedded) have severe power and area budgets. N:M sparsity can reduce inference compute and memory bandwidth by up to 16x at 1:16 ratio, but realizing this speedup requires ISA-level support that does not exist in commodity RISC-V cores.
method: A custom xDecimate ISA instruction is added to a RISC-V core that performs hardware-accelerated N:M sparse selection and MAC in a single operation. Decimate Im2col reformulates convolution to enable xDecimate on im2col-transformed feature maps. The MATCH compiler generates xDecimate-aware kernels. Synthesized at 22nm targeting the Vega PULP SoC (basis for commercial GAP9). Evaluated on ResNet-18 and ViT at 1:4, 1:8, and 1:16 sparsity ratios.
key_novelty: xDecimate: first RISC-V ISA extension specifically designed for N:M semi-structured sparsity, enabling hardware-level acceleration of 1:4 through 1:16 sparse patterns at only 5% area overhead on a commercial-grade SoC.
contributions: xDecimate custom RISC-V ISA instruction for N:M sparse MAC operations
Decimate Im2col algorithm adapting convolution to exploit xDecimate
MATCH compiler integration for automated xDecimate kernel generation
22nm synthesis showing 5% area overhead over baseline RISC-V core
3.21x speedup on ResNet-18 and 1.81x on ViT at 1:16 sparsity
Demonstration on Vega PULP SoC / GAP9 commercial product

metrics.speedup: 3.21x (ResNet-18) and 1.81x (ViT) at 1:16 sparsity vs dense baseline
metrics.area: 5% area overhead for xDecimate unit on 22nm RISC-V core
metrics.accuracy: Accuracy maintained within standard N:M sparsity training tolerances
metrics.other: 1:4 and 1:8 sparsity also evaluated with proportionally lower speedups

baselines: Software-only N:M sparsity on unmodified RISC-V
limitations: xDecimate requires retraining with N:M sparsity constraints
Speedup diminishes for ViT due to attention memory access patterns
Custom ISA extension requires toolchain modifications
Evaluation limited to two model architectures
